ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A smooth U-shaped metal track is fixed on a horizontal tabletop. The parallel segments of the track are separated by a distance $l$, and the rightmost end of the track is aligned with the right edge of the table. The resistance of the track is negligible. There is a uniform magnetic field with a magnetic flux density of magnitude $B$ directed vertically upwards in the region where the track is located. A metal rod $P$ with mass $m$, resistance $R$, and length $l$ is initially at rest on the track. An insulating rod $Q$ with mass $3m$ is located to the left of $P$ and moves toward $P$ with a speed $v_{0}$, undergoing an elastic collision with $P$. The duration of the collision is very short. After the collision, both $P$ and $Q$ slide off the right end of the track and land at the same point on the ground. While $P$ moves on the track, it maintains good contact with the track at both ends, and $P$ remains parallel to $Q$ at all times. Air resistance is negligible.

1. What is the magnitude of the velocity of the metal rod $P$ when it slides off the track?
2. What is the amount of heat generated in the metal rod $P$ during its motion on the track?
3. What is the time duration of the motion of the insulating rod $Q$ on the track after colliding with $P$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a horizontal tabletop, on which a U-shaped conducting rail is fixed. The two parallel parts of the rail extend to the right and at the right end are close to the edge of the table; in the rail region there are vertically upward magnetic-field arrows, marked as B. Two rods span between the parallel rails, the left one is marked Q, the right one is marked P, and the two remain parallel. In the figure the right end of the rail is connected with the edge of the table, indicating that the rods can slide out of the tabletop from the right end. Reasoning: The collision time is extremely short, so first consider only the one-dimensional elastic collision between Q and P. The mass of Q is 3m, and its initial velocity is v0; the mass of P is m, and it is initially at rest. After the elastic collision the velocities are u_Q=(3m-m)/(3m+m)·v0=v0/2, u_P=2·3m/(3m+m)·v0=3v0/2. Q is an insulating rod, and the rails and tabletop are smooth, so after the collision Q is not subjected to horizontal resistance and moves uniformly along the rails at v0/2 to the right end. The problem states that after P and Q slide out from the same right end, they fall to the same point on the ground. The vertical falling times of the two after leaving the table are the same, therefore their horizontal velocities when leaving the edge of the table must be equal. Therefore the magnitude of the velocity of the metal rod P when it slides out of the rails is v0/2. When P moves on the guide rails, the motional electromotive force is ε=Blv, the current is I=ε/R=Blv/R, and the magnitude of the Ampere resistance it experiences is F=BIl=B^2l^2v/R, with direction opposite to the direction of motion. P decelerates from the post-collision velocity 3v0/2 to the velocity v0/2 when leaving; all the reduced mechanical energy is converted into Joule heat in P, because the resistance of the guide rails is neglected. Therefore Q_heat=1/2·m[(3v0/2)^2-(v0/2)^2]=mv0^2. To find the motion time of Q on the rails after the collision, first find the distance from the collision point to the right end of the rails. For P there is m dv/dt=-(B^2l^2/R)v. Also dx/dt=v, so m dv/dx= -B^2l^2/R. Integrating from v=3v0/2 to v=v0/2 gives the distance x=mR/(B^2l^2)·(3v0/2-v0/2)=mRv0/(B^2l^2). Q travels the same distance uniformly at v0/2, so the time is t=x/(v0/2)=2mR/(B^2l^2).
